qs.q: An investigator analyzes frozen sections of adipose-rich tissue and needs to preserve neutral lipids without dissolving them during processing. Which stain must be utilized on unfixed frozen sections?
o: Oil Red O stain for intracellular lipid droplets
Toluidine blue stain for metachromatic granules
Fontana Masson stain for melanin pigment deposits
Warthin Starry stain for spirochete microorganisms
Luxol fast blue stain for central white matter
qs.e: Oil Red O is a lysochrome diazo dye used to stain neutral triglycerides and lipids in frozen sections.

qs.q: A pathology resident prepares unfixed frozen sections of skin to demonstrate lipid accumulation in a sebaceous lesion. Why must frozen sections be used?
qs.e: Routine histopathology processing utilizes alcohol and xylene solvents which dissolve neutral lipids out of the tissue.

qs.q: An investigator is analyzing frozen sections of adipose-rich tissue and needs to preserve and stain neutral lipids. Which stain must be utilized on these unfixed frozen sections?
qs.e: Oil Red O is used for neutral lipids and fats, specifically on frozen sections because routine paraffin processing dissolves fat. Haematoxylin and Eosin is the routine general stain for standard paraffin-embedded tissue.
